overview: Skyworks Solutions designs, manufactures, and markets analog and mixed-signal RF semiconductors -- amplifiers, filters, switches, front-end modules and related components -- used primarily in smartphones, with a growing secondary business in automotive, infrastructure, data center, Wi-Fi, and industrial/IoT applications. The company is headquartered in Irvine, California, and is one of the largest suppliers of RF front-end content for Apple's iPhone. Skyworks completed its approximately $22 billion cash-and-stock merger with rival Qorvo on October 5, 2026 (legacy Skyworks shareholders own ~63%, legacy Qorvo shareholders ~37% of the combined entity, which retains the Skyworks name and ticker), creating a larger, more diversified RF/analog semiconductor company with pro forma revenue of roughly $7.7B; starting with fiscal Q1 2027, results are reported on a fully combined basis across two segments, Smartphone and Diversified Growth Markets (DGM, formerly 'Broad Markets').

business_model.summary: Skyworks earns revenue selling RF front-end modules and discrete components to smartphone OEMs (primarily Apple) and, in its Broad Markets/DGM segment, to automotive, infrastructure, data center, Wi-Fi/networking, defense, and industrial/IoT customers. Revenue is transactional/design-win-driven rather than subscription-based: once a chip is designed into a device generation, Skyworks earns revenue each unit shipped for the life of that product cycle, but each new device generation is a fresh competitive bid. Standalone Mobile/Smartphone revenue was roughly 61% of FY2026 revenue (down from 66-69% in the prior two fiscal years, reflecting Apple's iPhone 17 dual-sourcing decision), with Broad Markets/DGM the remainder and growing faster (automotive, data center, and Wi-Fi 'growth engines' up double digits y/y in recent quarters). Post-merger, the combined company is guiding DGM to exceed 40% of sales, further diluting smartphone/Apple concentration at the consolidated level.

revenue_streams.name: Broad Markets / Diversified Growth Markets - automotive, infrastructure, data center, Wi-Fi, defense, IoT

business_model.customer_type: B2B - concentrated in a small number of large OEM customers (Apple is the single largest) for Mobile/Smartphone; broader base of industrial, automotive Tier-1, networking, and defense/aerospace customers for Broad Markets/DGM
business_model.geographic_mix: Revenue billed predominantly to Asia-based contract manufacturers and OEMs (China, Taiwan, South Korea) reflecting the global electronics supply chain, though end-demand is global; manufacturing/R&D concentrated in the US with assembly/test operations overseas

competitive_position.market_position: Post-merger, the combined Skyworks (incorporating former Qorvo) is a top-tier global RF front-end module supplier with pro forma revenue of ~$7.7B, positioning it closer in scale to Qualcomm (~21% global RFFE share, modem-RF integration strategy) and Broadcom (~18% share, FBAR filters and multi-year Apple supply agreements); standalone Skyworks and Qorvo each held roughly 5-6% share before combining, so the merger roughly doubles Skyworks' effective scale and product breadth (filters, PAs, switches, defense RF) without yet closing the gap to the two largest incumbents

moat_factors.description: Once designed into a device platform, RF content tends to persist for that generation, but OEMs (especially Apple) can and do re-bid sockets each generation and increasingly dual-source, eroding this advantage -- as demonstrated by the iPhone 17 content loss

moat_factors.factor: Technology/IP in filters and PA modules
moat_factors.description: Deep expertise in SAW/BAW filters, power amplifiers and module integration required for 5G/Wi-Fi 7 complexity; the Qorvo combination broadens the combined IP portfolio (including Qorvo's BAW filter and defense RF technology), but Broadcom's FBAR filter technology and Qualcomm's integrated modem-RF platform remain structurally stronger in premium sockets

Combined company targets $500M+ in annual cost synergies within 24-36 months of the October 5, 2026 close (an initial ~$150M of opex synergies targeted in FY2027, weighted to the second half, exiting at a $250-300M annualized run-rate), improving fab utilization and R&D leverage versus either company's prior standalone scale; Moody's upgraded the combined entity to investment-grade Baa3 and Fitch affirmed BBB+ with a stable outlook

Deep, long-standing Apple relationship provided volume certainty for over a decade, but the same concentration (Apple ~61% of FY2026 standalone Skyworks revenue, and a meaningful share of legacy Qorvo revenue too) is now actively working against the combined company as Apple diversifies its RF supply base

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a single customer (Apple) for the majority of revenue leaves the combined company exposed to sourcing decisions outside its control, even after the merger's diversification benefit
Loss of exclusive/majority RF socket share at Apple for the iPhone 17 (~20-25% content loss) demonstrates limited pricing/relationship power versus the customer
Smaller R&D and capex budget than Qualcomm or Broadcom even combined, which the Qorvo merger only partially addresses

Broad Markets/DGM diversification, while growing and now guided above 40% of combined sales, has not prevented consolidated revenue and GAAP earnings from falling sharply (FY2026 net income of $172.1M, GAAP diluted EPS $1.14, down from FY2025)

Newly elevated leverage (debt rose from $995.8M to $2,472.8M in the September 2026 quarter to fund the cash portion of the Qorvo deal) and dividend suspension reduce near-term capital-return flexibility

growth_drivers: Qorvo merger (closed October 5, 2026) creating a combined ~$7.7B pro forma revenue company with greater scale, broader product portfolio (adding Qorvo's BAW filters and defense/aerospace RF), and $500M+ targeted annual cost synergies within 24-36 months

Broad Markets/DGM diversification into automotive (ADAS, connectivity), data center/networking, Wi-Fi 7, defense/aerospace, and industrial IoT -- the combined DGM segment is guided to exceed 40% of sales in Q1 FY2027, growing high-single to low-double digits y/y on a combined basis
5G and Wi-Fi 7 content complexity increases dollar content per device even as unit growth is flat, benefiting suppliers who can integrate filters/PAs into higher-value modules
Defense/aerospace RF content (radar, EW, satellite communications), now larger post-merger given Qorvo's legacy defense exposure, is a smaller but higher-margin, less cyclical growth vector
Potential market share recovery or stabilization at Apple if dual-sourcing proves temporary or Skyworks wins back content in future iPhone generations
New $2 billion share repurchase authorization (running through January 2029) funded by capital freed from the suspended dividend, supporting EPS even amid topline softness
Post-merger cross-selling and combined customer relationships, particularly deepening non-Apple Mobile/Smartphone and DGM accounts

business.description: Apple represented roughly 61% of standalone Skyworks revenue in FY2026 (down from 66-69% in FY2024-25 but still the dominant customer); any shift in sourcing, pricing, or iPhone unit demand directly moves results. Apple's 2026 decision to dual-source a premier RF socket for iPhone 17 caused an estimated 20-25% RF content loss and triggered sharp analyst downgrades and price target cuts

business.risk: Smartphone unit cycle / RF content competition
business.description: Global smartphone unit growth is roughly flat-to-low-single-digit; the combined company must win RF content share each device generation against Qualcomm, Broadcom and emerging Chinese suppliers (MediaTek-ecosystem) rather than relying on market growth. Q1 FY2027 guidance calls for Smartphone revenue to fall in the low teens percent sequentially

business.risk: Revenue and earnings decline from prior peak
business.description: FY2026 standalone revenue was $3,959.6M (down from $4,086.9M in FY2025 and well below the ~$5.4-5.5B FY2021-22 peak); FY2026 GAAP net income was only $172.1M (diluted EPS $1.14) versus non-GAAP EPS of $5.05, reflecting heavy amortization, merger-related and other GAAP charges on top of the underlying revenue decline

business.risk: Customer-specific design loss risk extends beyond Apple
business.description: DGM customers are more numerous but each individual design win/loss at a large automotive or networking OEM can still be material to segment growth

financial.description: Debt rose from $995.8M to $2,472.8M in the September 2026 quarter after issuing ~$1,979.9M of long-term notes to fund the cash portion of the Qorvo deal ($32.50/share to Qorvo holders); net leverage at close was estimated at roughly 1.0x LTM adjusted EBITDA, and Q1 FY2027 EPS guidance embeds ~$50M of other expense, mainly acquisition-financing interest

The board suspended the quarterly cash dividend (last paid $0.71/share per quarter, $320.1M paid in FY2026 vs. $432.6M in FY2025) in July 2026 ahead of the merger close, redirecting capital to a new $2B buyback, deleveraging, and opportunistic M&A; no reinstatement timeline has been disclosed

financial.risk: Merger integration costs and synergy execution
financial.description: Only ~$150M of a targeted $500M+ in annual synergies is guided for FY2027 (weighted to H2, exiting at a $250-300M run-rate), leaving the bulk of the synergy case to execute over 2027-2029; integration of manufacturing footprints, product roadmaps and headcount carries real near-term cost and distraction risk
Foreign-sourced raw materials (including from China) and international manufacturing/test operations create modest FX and input-cost exposure

regulatory.risk: China export controls / entity list restrictions
regulatory.description: Expanding US export restrictions and additions to the BIS Entity List have limited and could further limit the company's ability to sell to certain Chinese entities and their business partners
US tariff actions and Chinese retaliatory countermeasures affect trade flows, costs, and demand given significant revenue billed through Asia-based supply chains

regulatory.risk: China rare earth / materials export controls
regulatory.description: Chinese rare-earth export controls pose industry-wide supply chain risk to semiconductor and electronics manufacturers, including RF component makers

macro.description: Smartphone revenue is tied to discretionary consumer upgrade cycles, which are sensitive to macro/consumer spending conditions

macro.risk: Semiconductor capital equipment and capacity cycles
macro.description: RF front-end demand for growth engines (data center, Wi-Fi, automotive) has recently run ahead of supply, a tailwind now but a capacity-driven margin risk if overbuilt

macro.risk: Interest rate sensitivity via new debt
macro.description: The company moved from a near-zero-net-debt position to over $2.4B of debt to fund the Qorvo acquisition, introducing new interest-rate sensitivity that did not exist standalone

execution.risk: Qorvo merger integration (now live, not pending)
execution.description: The combination closed October 5, 2026 and fiscal Q1 2027 is the first quarter of fully combined reporting (Smartphone/DGM segments); combining manufacturing footprints, product roadmaps, customer relationships, and headcount carries material execution risk; CEO Phil Brace leads the combined company with former Qorvo CEO Bob Bruggeworth on the board

New segment definitions (Smartphone, DGM) replace legacy Mobile/Broad Markets reporting starting Q1 FY2027, which may complicate near-term comparability and investor modeling during the integration period

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global RF front-end module market is maturing in smartphones (flat-to-low-single-digit unit growth) but increasing in per-device dollar content due to 5G/Wi-Fi 7 complexity; faster growth is occurring in automotive RF/connectivity, data center/networking, and defense/aerospace RF applications, which the combined Skyworks-Qorvo entity is now sized to pursue more aggressively via its DGM segment
macro_factors.cyclicality: High in Smartphone (tied to consumer upgrade cycles and a small number of large customers' design decisions); moderate-to-low in Broad Markets/DGM, which is more diversified across automotive, industrial, and infrastructure end markets and is guided to exceed 40% of combined revenue
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Previously low given minimal net debt; now moderate following the ~$2.5B of merger-related debt issuance, with Q1 FY2027 guidance embedding ~$50M of acquisition-financing interest expense per quarter
key_input_costs: Gallium arsenide and other compound semiconductor wafers
Rare earth and specialty materials subject to Chinese export controls

recent_developments.event: Reported fiscal Q4 and full-year FY2026 results (standalone, pre-merger close): Q4 revenue $1,045.7M (down from $1,100.2M y/y), GAAP diluted EPS $0.15, non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.28 (above guidance midpoint, vs. $1.76 y/y); FY2026 revenue $3,959.6M (down from $4,086.9M), GAAP diluted EPS $1.14, non-GAAP diluted EPS $5.05 (vs. $5.93 in FY2025); issued first combined-company guidance for Q1 FY2027 (December quarter): revenue of $1.80-1.90B (~$1.07B legacy Skyworks + ~$780M legacy Qorvo at midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS of ~$1.25 at the midpoint; Smartphone guided down low-teens percent sequentially, DGM up low-single digits sequentially and expected to exceed 40% of combined sales

Completed the approximately $22 billion cash-and-stock merger with Qorvo; combined company retains the Skyworks name and ticker (legacy Skyworks ~63% / legacy Qorvo ~37% ownership); management reiterated a target of $500M+ in annual cost synergies within 24-36 months, with ~$150M of opex synergies guided for FY2027 (weighted to H2) exiting at a $250-300M annualized run-rate; Moody's upgraded Skyworks to investment-grade Baa3 and Fitch affirmed BBB+ with a stable outlook

Issued approximately $1,979.9M of long-term notes (2028, 2032, and 2036 maturities) to fund the cash portion of the Qorvo merger consideration, raising total debt from $995.8M to roughly $2,472.8M by fiscal Q4 2026 quarter-end

Board suspended the quarterly cash dividend (last paid $0.71/share per quarter) ahead of the pending Qorvo merger and authorized a new $2 billion share repurchase program (running through January 2029), redirecting capital toward buybacks, deleveraging, and opportunistic M&A

Reported fiscal Q3 2026 results: revenue of $935M (above consensus), non-GAAP EPS of $1.08 (beat); Mobile revenue declined but Broad Markets grew, with Wi-Fi/data center/automotive 'growth engines' up a combined ~15% y/y; Apple's share of revenue fell to roughly 57% from ~63% a year earlier
Qorvo and Skyworks shareholders each approved the merger and related proposals at special stockholder meetings

Apple decided to dual-source a premier RF socket for the iPhone 17, resulting in an estimated 20-25% RF content loss for Skyworks at Apple; shares fell sharply and multiple analysts (Mizuho, Stifel, Citi, Morgan Stanley) cut ratings/price targets, with fair value estimates cut toward the $52-$74 range

Skyworks and Qorvo announced the definitive merger agreement: Qorvo holders to receive 0.960 Skyworks shares plus $32.50 cash per share; pro forma combined revenue of ~$7.7B and Adjusted EBITDA of ~$2.1B targeted, with $500M+ annual cost synergies expected within 24-36 months; Phil Brace (Skyworks CEO) to lead the combined company, Bob Bruggeworth (Qorvo CEO) to join the board

guidance.as_of: Q4/FY2026 Earnings (reported November 3, 2026) -- first guidance for the combined post-merger company
guidance.fiscal_year: FY2027 (fiscal year ends early October; first quarter of fully combined Smartphone/DGM reporting)

items.notes: Midpoint of ~$1.85B comprises roughly $1.07B legacy Skyworks and $780M legacy Qorvo; down ~7% sequentially from combined September-quarter revenue of ~$1.98B (~3% excluding Qorvo's extra reporting week)

Based on ~241M diluted shares and ~$50M of other expense (mainly acquisition-financing interest); SBC guided at $0.40-0.60/share, intangible amortization $0.45-0.65/share, tax items -$0.15 to $0.20/share
Reflects normal seasonal decline off the September quarter plus ongoing Apple content-loss impact

items.target: up low-single digits sequentially; high-single to low-double digits y/y combined
items.vs_prior: new segment definition replacing legacy 'Broad Markets'
items.notes: Guided to represent more than 40% of total combined-company sales

items.target: ~$150M of opex synergies in FY2027 (weighted to H2), exiting at a $250-300M annualized run-rate; $500M+ total within 24-36 months of close
items.vs_prior: maintained total target, added near-term phasing detail
items.notes: 24-36 month clock runs from the October 5, 2026 close

guidance.management_commentary: Management described Q4 FY2026 as a solid finish to the final standalone quarter, with results above the midpoint of guidance despite y/y revenue and non-GAAP EPS declines. On the Qorvo close, management emphasized the deal as 'a new chapter' for the combined company, reiterating $500M+ in targeted annual synergies and framing the DGM segment's move above 40% of sales as structurally reducing smartphone/Apple concentration. CFO commentary tied the elevated Q1 FY2027 other expense to acquisition-related financing and reiterated capital priorities of debt paydown, the new $2B buyback, and selective M&A following the dividend suspension.

bull_case: Qorvo merger (closed October 5, 2026) creates meaningful scale (~$7.7B pro forma revenue), diversifies Apple concentration as DGM is guided above 40% of combined sales, and targets $500M+ in annual cost synergies, with credit upgrades (Moody's Baa3, Fitch BBB+ stable) validating the combined balance sheet

Broad Markets/DGM 'growth engines' (Wi-Fi, data center, automotive) have been growing double digits with demand reportedly outstripping supply, providing a credible non-Apple growth vector now scaled up by Qorvo's product lines including defense/aerospace RF

Stock trades at a depressed valuation after the iPhone 17 content-loss selloff (analyst targets clustered roughly $52-$140, consensus near $75-$80), suggesting the market may already price in much of the near-term Apple content loss
New $2 billion buyback authorization (through January 2029) redirects capital previously paid as dividends toward EPS-supportive repurchases even as the dividend is suspended

Combined Skyworks-Qorvo becomes a larger, more credible global RF front-end supplier with broader IP portfolio (filters, PAs, defense RF) and improved negotiating leverage with OEM customers, with industry-wide 5G/Wi-Fi 7 content complexity raising RF dollar content per device even in a flat unit environment
bear_case: Apple's move to dual-source RF content for iPhone 17 (an estimated 20-25% content loss) may be the start of structural erosion of the company's most important customer relationship rather than a one-time event, with Apple still ~61% of standalone FY2026 revenue and Q1 FY2027 Smartphone guidance down low-teens percent sequentially

FY2026 GAAP net income fell to just $172.1M (diluted EPS $1.14) on revenue of $3,959.6M -- down from a ~$5.4-5.5B FY2021-22 revenue peak -- showing the underlying earnings base has compressed sharply even before merger integration costs are fully absorbed

The company took on roughly $1.5B+ of net new debt (debt rose from ~$996M to ~$2,473M) to fund the Qorvo cash consideration and suspended its dividend, reducing financial flexibility and introducing new interest-rate sensitivity just as the core business is shrinking

Large, complex merger integration carries meaningful execution risk, with only ~$150M of the $500M+ synergy target guided for FY2027 and the bulk of realization pushed out to 2028-2029, while new Smartphone/DGM segment reporting complicates near-term comparability for investors

Consensus analyst sentiment remains lukewarm (mostly Hold ratings, with price targets ranging as low as the $52-$74 area from several post-content-loss downgrades), and persistent China/US trade tensions, export controls, and tariff actions create ongoing supply chain and demand uncertainty given significant revenue billed through Asia-based OEMs and contract manufacturers

Even combined, the company remains smaller than Qualcomm and Broadcom in RF front-end share, and smartphone unit growth secularly remains flat-to-low-single-digit, capping the ceiling for the core Smartphone business
